title: Open findings — the standing row set the Court Gate reports on every run
whyThisLaneExists: courts/known-breaches.json enrolls a defect so the gate can stay green while it is reproduced EXACTLY as declared. That lane is correct for what it does and wrong as the only lane, because enrollment is terminal: an enrolled defect is described in prose, asserted by a court, and thereafter reported as an expected fact, so the next session opens a passing tree and writes another document. This file inverts the polarity. A row here asserts the REPAIR, not the defect. Its assertion fails while the finding is open and passes only when the repair has actually landed, at which point the gate reports RESOLVED and the row retires itself. Nobody marks a row done, so a finding cannot be closed by agreeing with it.
theDoneCondition: A row leaves this file when its assertion holds against the working tree, and by no other means. `status` may be set to "accepted" to keep a row that will not be repaired, but acceptance is a signed act: it requires both `acceptedBy` and `acceptedReason`, and scripts/verify-open-findings.ts refuses the file when either is missing. There is no disposition word a reader can assign to make a row stop counting.
whyThisFileIsData: This manifest carries no evaluation site. Assertions are declarative records naming a closed `kind` plus its operands; scripts/open-findings.mjs selects the predicate from a frozen set and refuses an unrecognized kind by name. No string in this file is ever compiled, evaluated, or executed as a command, glob, or pattern.
assertionKinds: The evaluator implements exactly three kinds: `fileContains` (path, needle) holds when the file exists and contains the literal needle; `fileLacks` (path, needle) holds when the file exists and does not contain it, so a deleted subject is a fault rather than a silent pass; `pathExists` (path) holds when the path is present. Needles are literal substrings, never regular expressions. Adding a kind means editing the evaluator and its verifier, which is the intended cost.
howToAddARow: An audit's deliverable is a row here, not a document. The prose belongs in archive/ as evidence; the row is what survives. A new row states the subject, one line of `what`, an assertion that is FALSE today and TRUE only after the repair, and an `assertionCeiling` naming what passing the assertion still does not prove.

findings.subject: aukora/broker/broker.mjs
findings.what: The broker does not retain the complete signed receipt as an artifact verifiable without signing-key access: Aura retains its signed claims and digest but omits the signature. The unchanged signer can reconstruct a matching receipt; that is not public-only retrieval. Existing issues #20 and #21 own retention and verification. A synthetic v3 brokerDispatch settlement at 2282bf9 returned a valid receipt and refused replay, while a regular-file scan of its fresh state found no copy of that receipt signature.

assertion.needle: Aura entries currently retain only a receipt

findings.assertionCeiling: This is a source-disclosure tripwire, not a behavioral proof: rewording the limitation can satisfy it without repairing retention. Honest closure requires a fresh-process verifier to recover the complete receipt from persisted state, check its digest against Aura and its signature against an independently expected signer, and reject missing, substituted, or corrupted receipts under restoration mutants. Retention alone does not sign checkpoints, provide external freshness, prove effect causation, or establish crash-atomic settlement.

findings.what: Six commits on 2026-08-29/30 (06f0b11, 88d5c5f, 60c8f36, 8d98289, a8c6d34, and a8c6d34's expected-row update) edited scripts/run-gate.mjs, scripts/run-gates.ts, and four independent courts, which ownership.theRule places outside builder authority: BUILDER/ORACLE SEPARATION IS ABSOLUTE. findings.subject: courts/known-breaches.json
findings.what: expectedBreachRows enrolls launch-ceremony P2 as red without naming which of its seven sub-predicates is red, and the court prints each row's observed detail truncated to 150 characters, so a sub-predicate flipping inside an enrolled-red row reaches no observer at all.
findings.assertionCeiling: Naming P2's red predicate records the reason once. It does not prove the gate compares sub-predicates on any run, does not cover this court's four other enrolled-red rows or the five other enrolled courts, does not lift the 150-character detail truncation that six courts share, and is satisfied by a prose sentence in `note` as readily as by a structured field. It also stays open if the custody defect is repaired and P2 becomes held without any predicate ever being named, which is correct: the hazard is the enrollment's row-level granularity, not P2's current state.

findings.subject: courts/harness/*/run.mjs
findings.what: Eighteen of the twenty-eight courts select their arm with exact-token argv tests and no usage guard, so a mistyped flag arms nothing, prints no diagnostic, and exits with the code the court would have produced anyway. Measured on all eighteen: --mutate=nonsense reproduced each court's plain-run exit code exactly (organism, proposal-namespace, live-dispatch, settlement, spine, seatbelt-reach, wasm-cell, wasm-proposal and wysiwys-issuer exit 0; amendment-channel, bearer-retirement, broker-proposal, composition-closure, escalation, executable-configuration, launch-ceremony, launch-ceremony-topology exit 1; uid-confinement exits 77 without root), and none emitted a usage or unknown-argument line. The guard at courts/harness/wasm-proposal-cell/run.mjs:27-30 exits 2 on the same input.
findings.assertionCeiling: The guard script naming the refusal exit proves someone wrote a guard. It does not prove the guard is wired into any gate, that every court adopted it, or that it fires: a stub carrying the needle in a comment satisfies this assertion, because the defect is an ABSENCE and no assertion kind in this manifest can express the absence of a guard. The strong form would need a predicate the evaluator runs, which this manifest deliberately forbids so that it carries no evaluation site. Read this row as a reminder, not as a check.
sources: measured 2026-08-30: all 18 unguarded courts run with --mutate=nonsense and --arm=bogus, exit codes captured directly

findings.subject: .oxlintrc.json
findings.what: oxlint lints none of the aukora/ organ tree: `ignorePatterns` excludes `**/*.mjs` outright, and every `overrides.files` glob is scoped to packages/*/*, apps/*, or examples/**, so the .d.mts companions match no rule set either. Measured on aukora/witness/attribution.d.mts: appending `export declare function probeUnusedRule(x: any): any` - a bare `any`, no JSDoc - and running `npx tsx scripts/run-oxlint.ts aukora/witness` printed nothing and exited 0, while the same runner reported five real findings on packages/governed/memory-put in the same session. A lint run against an organ path is therefore a green that measures nothing, and the only static signal covering aukora/ is whatever its hand-written .d.mts declares to a consuming spec.
findings.assertionCeiling: The blanket exclusion disappearing proves oxlint is no longer told to skip every .mjs file in the repository. It does not prove a rule set now matches aukora/, since every overrides.files glob is scoped to packages, apps and examples, and it does not prove any rule fires on organ source. The previous form of this row asserted the presence of an aukora glob, which an ignorePatterns entry satisfies while entrenching the defect.

findings.subject: packages/sandbox/sandbox-local/src/profiles.ts
findings.what: The drive assembly's discard regression fails only on Linux CI and only there: apps/web/tests/helix-capsule-broker.e2e.ts 'discards a started worker despite released late output' fails with ENOENT on the candidate tree's file, four times across PRs 222, 249, 257 and 289 in 2216-2507ms, while disposeGraceMs is demonstrably not the governing timer (289 raised it tenfold and changed nothing; the failing assertion carries its own timeout: 2000 poll). The mechanism is NOT established. An earlier version of this row asserted the confined worker is PID 1 of its own namespace and that its SIGTERM handler never runs; both are withdrawn. The repo's own implemented note .agents/notes/implemented/bug-fix/2026-08-06-bwrap-private-pid-namespace.md states that bubblewrap supplies the namespace's PID 1 process, so the worker is not PID 1, and the subprocess seam signals the process group. Candidate explanations that still fit: discard teardown ordering removing the tree before the late write; a --die-with-parent PR_SET_PDEATHSIG cascade killing the worker after its handler ran; or a timing flake. Distinguishing them needs a Linux runner with the worker's stdout/stderr surfaced.
findings.assertionCeiling: Passing records only that the drive assembly runs in the Court Gate. It does not prove the discard grace reaches a confined worker, does not prove the ENOENT is gone, does not identify the mechanism, and does not distinguish a repaired termination path from a relaxed expectation.

findings.subject: apps/cli/config/agent-presets/aukora/agent.cordis.yml
findings.what: The governed Web launch writes a measured literal disabling tool-bash and tool-pwsh at the profile layer (developer-launch.mjs webLiteralExecutableOverrides), but the preset it stages for the same launch re-enables tool-bash with disabled:false and also mounts tool-fs (read/write/edit), tool-fs-search, tool-jobs, tool-skill and tool-goal at the session layer. The live staged preset at ~/.dsh/aukora-governed/live/dsh-home/agent-presets/aukora/agent.cordis.yml carries all of these, and its own persona states that these native tools are not AUKORA-brokered effects, mint no Aura settlement receipts and do not all request an approval popup. The two layers disagree and nothing reconciles them, so reading the profile override alone misreports the deployment's actual tool surface. Separately, the session sandbox mode and approval policy are per-session state folded from the session log and survive restart by replay, so the launch literals are a default rather than a ceiling: the governed home's own projection cache holds 219 sessions of which 103 ran at danger-full-access and 162 at approval:never (inherited history, predominantly cwd /Users/peterviviani/aukora-harness and predating the 2026-09-13 cutover; none ran in the governed workspace).
findings.assertionCeiling: Passing records only that the governed Web profile names the shell tool its own staged preset mounts, so a reader of the profile is not misled about the tool surface. It does not prove the capability was removed, does not prove the two layers were reconciled, does not address the per-session sandbox/approval fold that makes the launch literals a default rather than a ceiling, and grades no tool manifest.

findings.subject: aukora/issuer/issuer.mjs
findings.what: No product code path calls the `approve-artifact` operation, so no owner/approval signature is ever produced for a real settlement. `handleApproveArtifact` is exported at aukora/issuer/issuer.mjs:702, dispatched from the op switch at aukora/issuer/issuer.mjs:450, and returns a signature at aukora/issuer/issuer.mjs:783 using `edSign(...)` over `approvalSignedMessage(artifactDigest)`. The only caller of `approve-artifact` anywhere in the repository is the test packages/governed/memory-put/tests/issuer-approval-artifact.spec.ts. Measured 2026-09-15 at branch head: outside that test, the operation appears only in the op switch and in documentation comments in aukora/receipt-v3/export.mjs and courts/harness/receipt-v3/run.mjs. Consequence for Receipt v3 step 1: every real export carries approval evidence that is absent, so its approval class is `unattributed`, it refuses `receipt:class-kind-mismatch`, and it can never be graded CONFORMING until an owner/approval signing path exists in a product caller.
findings.assertionCeiling: The absence of the string would not prove an approval path exists; it only means the operation name changed or moved.

findings.subject: aukora/issuer/issuer.mjs
findings.what: The approval signature the issuer produces is signed by the ISSUER ROOT key, not by an owner-held key, so it is issuer-attested approval evidence and does not establish owner-held key custody or physical human attendance. Measured at origin/main 022a732d: `handleApproveArtifact` (aukora/issuer/issuer.mjs:702) returns `edSign(null, approvalSignedMessage(artifactDigest), rootPrivateKey)` at aukora/issuer/issuer.mjs:783, and `rootPrivateKey` is the same root key the issuer uses for grants (loaded at aukora/issuer/issuer.mjs:213, used for the grant message at :636). The v3 verifier keeps the roles separate: `ownerPublicKeys` is a distinct trust input, and a `human-ceremony` document requires `approval.signerKeyId` to resolve inside it, refusing `approval:owner-key-unregistered` otherwise. The issuer root key is never placed in the owner role. Consequence for step 1: retaining this signature would provide issuer-attested approval evidence, but it must not be wired into the owner-signature role, and no owner-key registration, new signing channel, grant-family change or custody ceremony exists that would make a real export claim `human-ceremony`. Every real export is therefore `unattributed`.
findings.assertionCeiling: The absence of that string would not prove the signature moved to an owner key; it would only mean the signing call was rewritten.

findings.subject: aukora/supervisor/developer-web-bin.mjs
findings.what: With no --review-config, developer-web-bin.mjs:47-48 falls back to terminal review and calls createTerminalLines() even when process.stdin is not a terminal. Detached, readline closes at once; every later read rejects with the string "supervisor: approval input closed", which broker.mjs:3484 does not recognise and forwards to the child as the literal decision invalid, refused as broker:review-response-malformed. The launcher prints READY with no way to ask a human. The same readline fallback is copied in developer-terminal.mjs:20, developer-launch-bin.mjs:142 and developer-live-turn-bin.mjs:175.
findings.assertionCeiling: A launch-time refusal string proves the guard exists, not that a mid-session stdin close is forwarded as broker:review-channel-unavailable rather than invalid, and not that the three copies were collapsed into one helper; those need court rows with a pseudo-terminal and a closed pipe.
sources: External operator memo, 2026-09-16 (Will, via his own Claude read of aukora-deep at 5549c0e; confirmed by Fable against origin/main be2a5615)

findings.subject: aukora/broker/confinement.mjs
findings.what: confinement.mjs:398 refuses broker:seal-foreign-directory when the seal stateDev differs from the live stat, and macOS does not keep a volume device number stable across reboots. The refusal is designed (confinement court C13 stages exactly this case) and a sanctioned recovery exists (scripts/launchd-seal-recover.mjs replaces only stateDev after an attended decision with backup and stopped-writer check), but the refusal detail at confinement.mjs:403 prints two device numbers and nothing else. The external operator, told nothing, deleted the seal; repeated, that trains the reflex that would wave through a real directory swap.
findings.assertionCeiling: A recovery command named in the detail proves the message teaches, not that the named command works for the state directory in question; see seal-recovery-cli-installed-state-only. The verdict must not soften: same-inode device change keeps refusing.

findings.subject: scripts/launchd-seal-recover-bin.mjs
findings.what: The only seal-recovery CLI is hardwired to /private/var/db/aukora paths and requires darwin plus root (launchd-seal-recover-bin.mjs:12-16, :205). The library (recoverSealDevice) already admits the state owner uid, so developer state under a home directory, which is what 5173 runs on today, is recoverable in principle and has no command. No document under docs/ or README.md names seal recovery at all.
findings.assertionCeiling: A file existing is not a working recovery; the court must recover a same-inode device change on a developer-uid state directory and refuse an inode change, with the launchd variant unchanged.
